items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I worked with him then, and we went to the Apollo Theatre... working with Benny.

ctx.x: Let's see, Benny had four rhythm and three horn. A baritone saxophone, a trumpet and Benny played alto and trumpet, or whatever. You know, whatever he felt like playing. He played everything, you know. But a beautiful experience. And after we left there Benny formed a bigger band and I worked with him then, and we went to the Apollo Theatre, and this is where I got my greetings from Uncle Sam. And Benny -- I was so upset, and so Benny said, well John, look, I'm going to go before the board with you. And Benny…

But in the mean time Art had approached me about joining him with the trio, but you know, obviously I couldn't take the job because I had to go into the army, so I came back to New York on furlough and I went to see Art. He was working at this time at another club now, the Three Deuces, farther down the street. And this was in 1942. And Tiny Grimes was playing with him. And Art would tell me, John, please go over there and teach Tiny "Body and Soul", but Tiny was -- he just loved Charlie Christian, this is all he…
